title: Housing, living with others, autonomy and support at home
lede: A home can be inaccessible because of noise, layout, transport, living arrangements or the tasks required to maintain it. ‘Living independently’ can include daily support.

p: Indoor and outdoor noise, lighting, neighbours, transport, stairs, safety, whether there is a private space, visible storage, total cost and proximity to support. The cheapest home may be unworkable if it creates an enormous travel burden.

Home help, personal assistance, support with cleaning, food, shopping or money management, home automation and supported housing depending on the situation. Spain's dependency system aims to support an autonomous life in the person's usual environment where possible.
Agree in writing on tasks, noise, visitors, use of shared areas and what happens when someone needs to be alone. A useful household rule describes behaviours, not personal traits.

title: Family respite: what it is and how to request it
lede: Family respite provides hours of support, activities or short stays that allow people providing intensive support to rest or balance other responsibilities. It is not ‘abandoning care’: it can be part of a sustainable support network.

p: Common arrangements include support by the hour at home or in the community, supported leisure activities, weekends and short stays. Availability depends on the autonomous community, organisation and annual funding.

Ask the local organisation's Servicio de Apoyo a Familias, municipal social services or the regional network. It is useful to apply in advance because places for holidays and weekends often fill early.

Who the service accepts, staff ratios and training, healthcare support if needed, transport, cost, medication policy, communication during the stay and what happens if the person needs to return home early.

title: Family: change, siblings, parenthood and balancing responsibilities
lede: Moving home, separation, a birth, illness or a change of caregiver alters routines and relationships at the same time. Each family member may need different information and support.

p: Say what will change, what will stay the same and when it will happen. Use a calendar or photographs if they help. Do not promise that ‘everything will stay the same’ if that is not true.

Do not turn a sibling into a caregiver by default. They can contribute like any other family member, but they need their own time, age-appropriate information and the right to express anger or tiredness without feeling guilty.
Simplify logistics, share calendars, automate shopping, accept outside support and protect recovery time. A parent's need for support does not invalidate their ability to parent.

title: Free communication tools and pictograms
lede: Augmentative and alternative communication includes many tools: boards, pictograms, text, keyboards, signs, synthesised speech and devices. Pictograms are one option, not a compulsory system for everyone.

p: ARASAAC provides pictograms and materials for communication and cognitive accessibility. Communication devices and digital planners can also combine images, photographs, text and speech. The tool should match the person's motor access, vision, reading, language and preferences.

A person who uses AAC needs access to their system throughout the day, including at school, in hospital, during leisure activities and in stressful situations. Taking the device away because it ‘distracts’ them is equivalent to removing a means of communication.

ARASAAC resources are distributed under a CC BY-NC-SA licence and the terms of use exclude commercial use without permission. For that reason, free downloads should be kept clearly separate from commercial materials.

title: Legal support after turning 18
lede: Since the reform introduced by Ley 8/2021, an adult retains legal capacity. When they need help to exercise it, the system is based on support and on respecting their wishes, preferences and choices.

p: The official Spanish figure of guarda de hecho can cover everyday support without a formal judicial measure; voluntary measures allow the person themselves to arrange before a notary who they want to support them and how; and curatela is a judicial support measure, normally assistive, with representation reserved for specific exceptional cases.

A legal support arrangement is not chosen on diagnosis alone. The relevant questions are which decisions the person can make independently, which they can make with accessible information, where they need someone alongside them and whether there are conflicts of interest.

Check the effect on benefits, tax relief, banking and administrative procedures already in place. For an individual decision, it is advisable to use a specialist legal service; this entry is for guidance.

title: Finding an association by condition and region
lede: Not all 185 concepts have their own federation. Where an association network exists, the national organisation is often the best starting point for finding regional or provincial associations and learning what services are available.

p: Start with the national federation or confederation and check its list of member organisations. For autism: Confederación Autismo España and FESPAU; for intellectual and developmental disability: Plena inclusión. For other conditions, look for the relevant national federation and check that the organisation remains active and its contact details are current.

Guidance on administrative procedures, support groups, leisure activities, respite, employment, training, family support or referrals to local resources. Each organisation has different eligibility criteria, funding and waiting lists.

The website links to organisations and sources; it does not certify treatments or turn an association into a clinical authority. Each entry should state the geographical area and the date on which the link was checked.

title: Bullying, discrimination and racism: how to respond
lede: Bullying and discrimination are not ‘social-skills problems’ belonging to the person targeted. The person needs protection, the events need to be recorded and the appropriate route for the setting needs to be used.

p: Record the date, place, what happened, who was present, screenshots or messages, and who was informed. Describing specific behaviour prevents the case from being reduced to ‘they do not get along’.

At school: the school's convivencia/bullying protocol and senior management. At work: the employer, occupational health or human resources, employee representation or the labour inspectorate as appropriate. For services open to the public: make a complaint and, where appropriate, use administrative or legal routes. If there is a threat or criminal offence, contact Policía Nacional or Guardia Civil.

Ley 15/2022 protects against discrimination in employment, education, healthcare, transport, culture, housing, goods and services, the internet and other areas. Disability also has specific protection under RDL 1/2013.

title: Money, contracts, forms and administrative procedures
lede: Managing money and administration combines dates, reading, calculation, memory, passwords and decisions. Support can be occasional without removing the person's autonomy over decisions.

p: Set up direct debits for regular payments, limit the number of accounts, turn on alerts, separate money for fixed and variable expenses, and keep contracts in one folder. For administrative procedures, a list of the ‘documents they always ask for’ avoids starting from scratch each time.
Disabled people have a right to accessibility and, in relation to goods and services, to information in appropriate formats and reasonable and proportionate measures.

Distinguish support from substitution: reading a letter, explaining options or accompanying someone to an appointment does not mean deciding for them. If stable legal support is needed, link to the entry on legal support after turning 18.
